claims.text: All Kubernetes objects are stored in etcd; an etcd snapshot file contains all the Kubernetes state, and restoring it returns the cluster's objects to the moment it was taken.
etcd members replicate every accepted write, so a deletion accepted by the cluster reaches all members; more members do not protect against a wrong change.
claims.source_hint: etcd docs v3.6 FAQ / failure modes (replicated log); k8s.l3.control-plane-ha claims on quorum

claims.text: etcdctl is a client that talks to a running etcd over the network; etcdutl operates directly on etcd data files, used for snapshot restore and status.
etcdctl snapshot save takes a snapshot from a live member through its client endpoint, given --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 and --cacert/--cert/--key.
claims.source_hint: configure-upgrade-etcd.md 'Built-in snapshot' and 'Snapshot using etcdctl options' (lines 296-308, 378-383)

claims.text: etcd's client port in a kubeadm cluster is 2379 and its peer port 2380; etcd trusts client certificates signed by the etcd CA kubeadm created in /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd (ca.crt, server.crt, server.key, passed only to etcdctl in the script).
claims.source_hint: PKI certificates and requirements (etcd/ca, paths); ports-and-protocols.md (2379-2380); scripts/lib/lifecycle.sh etcd_tls @ stage-3

claims.text: On a kubeadm node, etcd's data directory is /var/lib/etcd, mounted into the etcd static Pod from the node (hostPath volume etcd-data).
claims.source_hint: configure-upgrade-etcd.md line 451 (etcd.yaml volumes.hostPath etcd-data); deploy/k8s/kind-lifecycle-config.yaml lines 4-5 @ stage-3

claims.text: etcdutl snapshot restore writes a new data directory given by --data-dir, for a member given by --name and its peer URL (--initial-cluster, --initial-advertise-peer-urls); the running etcd keeps using its own until restarted on the new one.
claims.source_hint: configure-upgrade-etcd.md 'Restoring an etcd cluster' (lines 426-451); etcd v3.6 op-guide/recovery (restore flags)

claims.text: Stop all API servers, restore etcd, restart the API servers; the docs also recommend restarting kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager and kubelet so they don't rely on stale data. The lab restarts only etcd and the API server.
The kubelet stops a static Pod when its manifest is removed from the watched folder (/etc/kubernetes/manifests) and starts it again when the file is put back.
claims.source_hint: tasks/configure-pod-container/static-pod.md 'Dynamic addition and removal of static pods'

claims.text: etcd-snapshot.sh: creates donhang-lifecycle (kind: one control-plane node, a Docker container, set up by kubeadm, v1.34.11), ConfigMap before, snapshot, docker cp to backups/etcd/donhang-lifecycle.db, ConfigMap after; restore; swaps member folders.
claims.source_hint: scripts/k8s/etcd-snapshot.sh lines 8-60, scripts/lib/lifecycle.sh, deploy/k8s/kind-lifecycle-config.yaml @ stage-3; kind docs (node containers bootstrapped with kubeadm)

claims.text: After the restore, kubectl get configmaps before after lists before and returns Error from server (NotFound): configmaps "after" not found.

etcd holds API objects (including PersistentVolumeClaim and PersistentVolume objects, and image names in Pod specs) but not the data on the volumes or the images in the registry; those need their own backups.
claims.source_hint: configure-upgrade-etcd.md 'Backing up' (Kubernetes objects); concepts/storage/persistent-volumes.md (PV backed by external storage)

claims.text: By default Secrets are stored unencrypted in etcd, so a snapshot file exposes them; the Kubernetes docs advise encrypting snapshot files.
claims.source_hint: concepts/configuration/secret.md caution ('stored unencrypted in the API server's underlying data store (etcd)'); configure-upgrade-etcd.md line 289

claims.text: A snapshot left only on the node is lost with the node, so copy it off the node.
claims.source_hint: scripts/k8s/etcd-snapshot.sh line 22 @ stage-3; general backup practice

claims.text: When lost objects are in the config repository, re-syncing them with Argo CD recreates them without undoing changes made since the last snapshot, so it is the smaller repair; objects that exist only in the cluster come back only from a snapshot.

Controllers compare objects with what exists, so after a restore they work from the rewound objects; the Kubernetes docs recommend restarting kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager and the kubelet so none of them keeps stale data.
claims.source_hint: concepts/architecture/controller.md (control loop); configure-upgrade-etcd.md lines 409-412 (restart components, stale data)
